correctness.rationale: Each signed basis contributes product over chosen negative points (1−2). Summing the expansion over independent k-subsets gives W_r(S)=sum_{k=0}^r (-2)^k c_k(S) N_k(r), with N_k(r)=prod_{j=k}^{r−1}(2^r−2^j)/(r−k)!. For r≥5 the exact valuation v2(2^k N_k)=k+(r−k)(r+k−1)/2−v2((r−k)!) exceeds r for k<r and equals r for k=r; hence W_r(S)≡(-2)^r c_r(S) mod 2^{r+1}, and a basis-sized S attains valuation r. For r=3,4 the extension counts yield constant residue 4 mod 8 and 8 mod 16, forcing nonzero all frequencies; r=1,2 multipliers odd. At r=5 the frequency (span(e1,e2,e3)\{0})∪{e4,e5} has independent-set counts (1,9,36,77,77,28), and exact extension counts (83328,13440,1792,192,16,1), whose signed sum is exactly zero. Read pg_basis_fourier_check.py which exhausts rank-four 32768 Walsh characters and directly counts rank-five 83328 bases; independently checked the finite cancellation and formula. Symbolic valuation proves all-rank claims, not enumeration through rank64.
